title: asset-optimization
description: Learn about asset-optimization. Master the concepts, patterns, and best practices.

data.text: Asset optimization involves transforming images, fonts, and other media files to reduce their size while maintaining quality. Optimized assets load faster, use less bandwidth, and improve overall application performance.
Images are often the largest resources on a web page. Optimization includes choosing the right format, compressing appropriately, serving responsive sizes, and implementing lazy loading.

data.title: Modern Image Formats
data.code:
Image Format Comparison (same image quality):

Original PNG: 2.5MB
JPEG (80% quality): 250KB (90% reduction)
WebP (lossy): 180KB (93% reduction)
AVIF (lossy): 120KB (95% reduction)

Format Recommendations:
- Photographs: WebP/AVIF with JPEG fallback
- Graphics: SVG or PNG with WebP fallback
- Icons: SVG or WebP
- Screenshots: WebP or JPEG

Format Support:
- WebP: 95%+ browsers
- AVIF: 70%+ browsers (growing)
- JPEG: Universal support
- PNG: Universal support

data.text: Serve appropriately sized images based on the user's device and viewport. This prevents mobile users from downloading desktop-sized images they don't need.

data.text: Fonts can significantly impact page load performance. Optimize fonts by using modern formats, subsetting, implementing proper loading strategies, and preventing layout shifts.

data.title: Font Optimization Techniques
data.code:
Font Optimization Techniques:

1. Use Modern Formats
   - WOFF2 (30% better than WOFF)
 - WOFF2 with WOFF fallback

2. Subset Fonts
   - Include only characters you use
   - Reduces font file size by 60-90%
   - Use glyphhanger or similar tools

3. Font Loading Strategy
   - Use font-display: swap for instant text
   - Preload critical fonts
   - Avoid @font-face blocking

4. Font Loading Order
   - Preload critical above-fold fonts
   - Lazy load other fonts
   - Use font face with local()

5. Variable Fonts
   - Single file instead of multiple weights
   - Better compression and loading
   - More flexible design system

data.title: Font Loading Implementation
data.code:
<!-- Preload critical fonts -->
<link rel="preload" href="/fonts/main.woff2" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin>

<!-- Font with swap strategy -->
<style>
@font-face {
  font-family: 'Main Font';
  src: url('/fonts/main.woff2') format('woff2');
  font-display: swap; /* Show fallback immediately */
}

body {
  font-family: 'Main Font', system-ui, sans-serif;
}
</style>

<!-- Reserve space to prevent layout shift -->
.hero-title {
  font-family: 'Main Font', system-ui, sans-serif;
  font-size: 2.5rem;
  aspect-ratio: 10/3; /* Reserve space */
}

data.text: Videos are the heaviest assets on most pages. Optimize by using modern codecs, adaptive streaming, appropriate resolution, and lazy loading.

data.title: Video Optimization Best Practices
data.code:
Video Optimization Best Practices:

1. Modern Codecs
   - H.264 (universal support)
   - VP9 (better compression, wide support)
   - AVIF (best compression, growing support)

2. Adaptive Streaming
   - DASH or HLS for adaptive quality
   - Adjusts based on network conditions
   - Reduces buffering and improves UX

3. Lazy Loading
   - Load video only when scrolled into view
   - Use loading="lazy" attribute
   - Load poster image first

4. Responsive Quality
   - Serve different resolutions
   - 720p for mobile, 1080p for desktop
   - Use bitrate adaptation

5. Autoplay Considerations
   - Disable autoplay (bandwidth intensive)
   - Use muted autoplay if needed
   - Respect prefers-reduced-motion

Implementation:
<video 
  controls
  preload="none"
  poster="poster.jpg"
  loading="lazy"
  playsinline
>
  <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <source src="video.webm" type="video/webm">
  Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>

data.text: Implement proper caching headers for assets to avoid unnecessary network requests while ensuring updates are delivered when needed.

data.title: Asset Caching Configuration
data.content: Set appropriate cache headers for different asset types.
data.code:
Cache Header Strategies:

1. Static Assets (CSS, JS, images)
   - Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable
   - Content hashes for cache busting
   - CDN caching for global distribution

2. Versioned Assets
   - /assets/v1/image.jpg
   - Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable
   - Change version when updating files

3. Frequently Updated Assets
   - Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600
   - Short cache time to allow updates
   - Use ETag for revalidation

4. User-Generated Content
   - Cache-Control: private, max-age=300
   - ETag for revalidation
   - Avoid caching sensitive data

Implementation:
# nginx configuration
location ~*\.(jpg|jpeg|png|gif|webp|svg|woff|woff2)$ {
  expires 1y;
  add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable";
}

location ~*\.(css|js)$ {
  expires 1y;
  add_header Cache-Control "public, immutable";
}

data.title: Image Quality Trade-offs
data.text: Don't over-optimize images at the expense of quality. Find the right balance between file size and visual quality for your use case. Test different quality settings to find the optimal point.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Optimize images with modern formats (WebP/AVIF) and responsive sizing
Subset fonts to include only characters you actually use
Use WOFF2 font format with WOFF fallback for better compression
Implement font-display: swap to prevent invisible text
Optimize videos with modern codecs and adaptive streaming
Set appropriate cache headers for different asset types
Automate asset optimization in your build process
Balance file size reduction with quality requirements
data.takeaway: Asset optimization is high-impact for web performance, with image and font optimization often providing the biggest wins for reducing page load times.
